title: Engine
description: What the trading engine is doing. Cycle liveness and outcome, the intent it emitted, the book composition behind that intent, and the journal retention the next cycle's deltas depend on. Every number here is INTENDED state — what the engine decided, never what the market did; realized state lives in the engine journal on the capture primary.

panels.title: Intent vs execution — read the right row

options.content: **Two kinds of numbers live on this board.** The Intent and Composition rows are the engine's *decisions* — target weights and intended orders, computed every cycle whether or not anything may trade. The Execution row is what actually *happened* at the venue — orders, fills, fees, positions, realized PnL — published by the execution path and reading flat zero, not absent, outside an attended trading window. The Venue truth row is what the exchange said we could trade and held at each cycle. An intended order with no fill beside it is the normal shadow state, not a failure. A resting order is one execution number that can appear without any trading: the `rest-hold` mode places a real order at the venue on purpose and leaves it there for a drill to act on. Read the mode label before reading activity as trading.

panels.title: Last cycle age
panels.description: How long since the trading engine last completed a cycle — the single glance that says whether the four-hourly loop is still turning. Pages above 16500 s (4h35m) after `for: 5m`, and the line drawn here is that alert's own bar. A healthy cycle completes within 30 minutes of its boundary, so the worst legitimate age is 4h30m — reached just before the next cycle lands — and the bar sits five minutes past it; anything above the line is a stopped or crash-looping engine, not a slow one. **This is the one rule on this board that also pages on ABSENCE**: the gauge is seeded at engine start from the newest journal artifact, so it is never legitimately missing while the engine runs, and a vanished series means the engine itself is gone. The tile therefore reads NO CYCLE DATA **in red** when the series disappears — unlike the outcome reading beside it, absence here is a fault and not a value the engine is declining to publish. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Last cycle outcome — absent is NOT failure
panels.description: Did the most recent cycle succeed, fail, or has the engine not determined an outcome yet — three distinct states, rendered as three. Pages the moment this reads 0, with no pending period (`for: 0s`): the outcome is final as soon as it is published, because the engine never re-runs a boundary that already has a journal artifact, so a pending window would buy silence and nothing else. **NO OUTCOME YET is not a failure** — the engine deliberately publishes nothing until it has actually measured an outcome, so a fresh start or an unreadable journal shows this state and does not page. That is why the colour here comes from value mappings and not from a threshold ladder: a ladder would paint honest absence red, inventing exactly the claim the engine refuses to publish. The cycle-age reading beside this one cannot cover this question — the metrics sink refreshes the completion timestamp after a FAILED cycle too, so age stays green while every cycle fails. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Engine exporter scrape (:9102)
panels.description: The absent-versus-dark discriminator that makes the two readings beside it interpretable. SCRAPING means the telemetry agent is reaching the engine's exporter, so a missing engine series is honest absence. NOT LISTENING means the agent is alive and the engine is not answering on its port. NO SCRAPE DATA means this machine's agent stopped shipping and every panel on this board is blind — it is left neutral rather than red, because absence is not a value this board is willing to colour. No alert reads this tile: a per-target scrape failure surfaces as the cycle-age page on the left, and the machine-wide dark case is owned by the fleet board, whose rule counts series presence and stays satisfied while this one target reads 0.

panels.title: Cycle cadence — age sawtooth
panels.description: Six teeth a day. Each tooth rises to at most 4h30m and drops when the next cycle completes. A missing tooth is a skipped boundary and a tooth that overtops the line is a late one — neither of which a point-in-time reading can show, which is the whole reason this panel sits beside the stat. Same series and same bar as the cycle-age reading above, which owns the alert pointer; the page fires after `for: 5m` above the line. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Cycle duration — wall time per cycle
panels.description: Is a cycle creeping toward the deadlines that otherwise surface first as an unexplained failed cycle? **The line drawn here is the engine's own 25-minute refresh reserve, not an alert bar** — past it the cycle's transport and settle retries stop, and nothing in the fleet pages on this number; the failure it predicts pages as a failed cycle. A completion is expected to land within 30 minutes of its boundary, so a cycle approaching that second figure is already spending the whole window. This series is **absent, not zero**, until the first cycle of a fresh process completes: the engine will not publish a duration it has not measured, so an empty chart after a restart is the honest state and not a gap to fill in. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Intended trade activity — last 24h (decisions, not fills)
panels.description: Did the engine intend to trade today, and for how much — the headline number for a shadow book. **Decisions, not fills**: nothing on this board observes execution, and these two numbers count orders the engine emitted an intention for. Deliberately carries no colour at all — nothing pages on intent volume, and green or red on a trade count would assert a judgement no rule in this fleet has made. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Intended orders — cumulative & rolling 24h
panels.description: The recent-delta pairing for order count: the cumulative line answers *has the engine ever intended to trade*, the rolling 24h line answers *is it intending to trade now*. **Decisions, not fills.** The cumulative series is on the right axis — the two live on completely different scales — and a process restart drops it back to zero, which the restart markers on the time axis are what distinguish from a real reset. No alert reads either line. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Intended order notional — cumulative & rolling 24h
panels.description: The euro weight of the day's intentions, so a day of many small rebalances is distinguishable from one large one. **Decisions, not fills** — this is notional the engine intended to move, not notional that moved. The cumulative series is on the right axis and drops back to zero on a process restart; the restart markers on the time axis show when. No alert reads either line. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Target weights by asset — INTENDED allocation (not held)
panels.description: How the intended book is allocated and how that has moved. **These are target weights the engine computed, not holdings.** Stacked, so an asset entering or leaving the target set is legible as a band appearing or collapsing. An asset that leaves the set has its series removed rather than zeroed — a zero weight and a not-in-the-book asset are different states — so a band ends instead of flattening onto the axis. An empty chart means no cycle has published a target set since the process started, which the cycle-age reading at the top of this board will explain. No alert reads this panel. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Target weights — latest cycle (intent snapshot)
panels.description: Exactly which assets the last cycle targeted and at what weight — the view to read before touching anything. **Intent, not holdings.** Deliberately uncoloured: a target weight has no good or bad value and no rule reads one. An empty panel here means no cycle has published a target set since the process started, which the cycle-age reading at the top of this board will explain. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Active sleeves & composition changes (26h)
panels.description: The alerted series, plotted exactly as the rule evaluates it, so the page and this panel show the same number. Any step in the active-sleeve count — a dormant sleeve arming, or an active one going flat — is the event: the count is not monotone and the direction does not matter, because both directions move portfolio gross materially. Pages above 0 after `for: 5m`, and the line sits at 1 because the counting function is integer-valued and 1 is the first value that trips the bar; a line at 0 would paint every healthy sample red. The 26-hour window is wider than a day so the page ages out on its own. The raw count is context on the right axis and carries no line. This family has exactly one publisher — the trading engine on the capture primary — which is why the alerted expression needs no machine matcher and carries none. The count itself is **absent, not zero**, until a cycle has actually measured a composition.

panels.title: Sleeve gross — per sleeve (intended exposure)
panels.description: **Which** sleeve moved — the follow-up view for the composition alert, and literally where that alert's summary sends the reader. Per-sleeve gross is the sum of that sleeve's absolute target weights, so a sleeve sitting flat at zero for months is correct behaviour for a long-only sleeve in a sustained downtrend, and its re-arming is the event the alert announces. **Intended exposure, not held.** The alert pointer is on the panel to the left, which plots the alert's own value; nothing pages on this one. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Book-level intent — net vs gross target weight
panels.description: The quantitative consequence the composition alert warns about. A dormant sleeve re-arming changes what the book IS; it does not by itself tell you gross moved (measured 2026-08-22: the count went 1 to 3 while the book rose x1.15, then fell below its starting point) and invalidates the drift band derived under the previous composition, and this is the line on which that is measurable; the distance between net and gross is the book's directional lean. **Intended weights, not held.** Nothing alerts on either line, so neither carries a bar. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Journal prune freshness — script clock vs published file age
panels.description: Is the daily journal prune still running, and do the script and the collector agree? The two normally track within seconds; a gap between them means the script ran but its metrics file was not written or not readable. **A stale metrics file is not a scrape error** — the collector keeps serving the last values forever, so without this panel the retention numbers beside it would read healthy indefinitely. The line at 26 hours sits on the published-file series only; both series now carry a rule, the published-file age paging above that bar after `for: 30m` and the script clock alarming on its own absence, so the bar reads for one of the two and not for the other. That expression is written exactly as the alert evaluates it, which is why its matcher covers both capture machines even though only the primary runs the prune — the secondary contributes no series and that single line is the expected result, not a broken query. The alert pointer for this signal lives on the fleet board, which carries both metrics-file slices with their own bars.

panels.title: Journal retention — day-dirs kept vs deleted per run
panels.description: Is the 60-day journal tail intact? A collapsing kept-count is the one housekeeping failure that changes what the engine **trades**: below two retained day-directories the next cycle's delta derivation degenerates into a full-book rebuild, because there is no prior record to take the delta against. **The line at two day-directories is that floor, not an alert bar** — nothing pages on it today, and this panel is the visibility that has to exist before a rule can. Retention is configured at 60 days, so the kept count settles just above that and a slow decline is the shape to watch for. The deleted count is on the right axis and carries no line: a run with nothing to remove correctly reports zero. Both series come from the prune script's metrics file on the capture primary, refreshed once a day — so on a freshly provisioned machine this panel is empty until that daily run first fires, which is honest absence and not a broken query.

panels.title: Oldest retained journal day
panels.description: Is the prune actually deleting, or only running? Kept-day count and last-run time are process measures; the age of the oldest surviving day-directory is the outcome measure. With retention configured at 60 days it should sit just past that figure and stay there — a value that keeps climbing means the script runs, reports success and removes nothing, which no other series on this board would reveal. **The line at two days is the same floor the panel beside this one draws, not an alert bar**: below it the journal tail has collapsed and the next cycle rebuilds the whole book instead of taking a delta. No upper bar is drawn, because the healthy value sits a little above the retention figure by construction and a line there would read red on a correct prune. Published from the prune script's metrics file on the capture primary, refreshed once a day — so on a freshly provisioned machine this panel is empty until that daily run first fires.

panels.title: Execution gate level
panels.description: What the engine may submit right now, decoded from the raw 0/1/2 the gate publishes: 0 = nothing may be submitted, 1 = reducing orders only, 2 = anything. This is the SUMMARY the gate computed from the four inputs beside it (armed, kill switch, restart hold, venue) -- it says THAT the envelope sits at a given level, never WHICH input put it there, because `reasons` never reaches Grafana and this board cannot show it. Read `zcrypto engine exec-status` on the engine host for the full breakdown. No alert reads this tile directly -- the two conditions that matter most, an unexpected arm and a tripped kill switch, have their own rules on the tiles beside it. Absence here means the exporter itself is gone, the same fault the cycle-age reading at the top of this board covers. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Order submission armed
panels.description: Whether BOTH arming keys are present: the `armed` config flag and the arm file on the engine host. Deliberately conflated into one gauge -- this tile can say THAT the engine is armed or disarmed, never WHICH of the two keys is set, so `zcrypto engine exec-status` on the host is the next step whenever this needs explaining. Pages after six continuous hours armed, because arming is expected only inside an attended probe window and is normally removed when the window ends -- an armed reading is not itself an incident, but it removes one of the two keys standing between a mistake and real money. Runbook: infra/runbooks/engine.md#zcrypto-engine-exec-armed-too-long. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Execution kill switch
panels.description: Whether the kill-switch file is present on the engine host. TRIPPED means the engine refuses every order regardless of any other reading on this row. This is a deliberate control, not a fault by itself -- deleting the kill file on the engine host clears it immediately, with no deploy and no restart. The alert beside it pages after 5 minutes tripped, because the failure mode it guards against is forgetting to remove the file, not tripping it. Runbook: infra/runbooks/engine.md#zcrypto-engine-exec-kill-tripped. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Restart hold (reduce-only latch)
panels.description: Whether this process is still latched to reduce-only after its most recent restart. Written unconditionally on every engine start and cleared only by a human -- nothing in the gate clears it on its own. HELD is the expected reading immediately after any restart (a converge, a supervisor healing a start the node aborted, a reboot). No alert reads this tile directly; it is one of the four inputs behind the gate-level reading beside it. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Venue status — last evaluated reading
panels.description: Whether the engine's own last read of the Kraken system status said the venue is online. It moves ONLY when the execution gate is evaluated -- at process start, after each cycle (roughly four-hourly), and on every tick while a plan is running; an idle engine reads no gate at all. So between cycles this reading can be hours old, in EITHER direction: ONLINE right through a venue outage the capture side is already paging on, or NOT ONLINE long after the venue came back. The gate evaluation heartbeat beside it is this tile's age -- read the two together or neither. A stale tile is never a stale gate: every submission evaluates the gate itself first, on a venue read cached at most 30 seconds, before any order goes out. NOT ONLINE forces the gate level to 0 regardless of arming. This is a gating INPUT, not the venue alert itself: `Capture · Kraken reports the venue is not online` already pages on the underlying condition from the capture side, so this tile carries no alert of its own -- one would only double-page the same event. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Gate evaluation heartbeat
panels.description: How long since the execution gate was last evaluated -- the heartbeat that makes every other tile on this row trustworthy. The gate runs at process start and after every cycle, roughly four-hourly, so a healthy reading tracks the cycle-age reading at the top of this board. If this stops advancing, EVERY gauge on this row freezes at its last value: cycle telemetry can stay perfectly healthy while the safety envelope is silently no longer being read at all. Pages above 17100s (4h45m) after `for: 10m`, including on absence -- a gate that never published at all is this alert's worst case, not an exemption from it. Runbook: infra/runbooks/engine.md#zcrypto-engine-exec-not-evaluated. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary, and the expression carries that machine's own matcher because the alert does.

panels.title: Weekly tracking error — last verdict
panels.description: What the engine decided about the most recently closed week, re-derived at every 4-hourly boundary from the journal alone. DISARMED means no band is configured, so nothing is measured against one -- the resting state, and the state to confirm after a deploy that was not meant to arm anything. NOT SCORED means the week could not be judged: short of its full 42 boundaries, spent below the full gate level, straddling the first fill ever, or missing the prices it was traded at -- all deliberate refusals, never a pass. WITHIN BAND is the healthy reading. OUTSIDE BAND means the week's mean drift from target exceeded the band and the kill switch has latched, which pages through the kill-switch alert beside it rather than through a rule of its own. The series is absent until the first boundary after a start, because before that there is no verdict to state. Runbook: infra/runbooks/engine-procedures.md#engine-tracking-band. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Execution — what actually happened at the venue
Orders by outcome, and external order events
panels.description: Orders the executor submitted to the venue, split by what happened to each: submitted, accepted, rejected, venue_canceled (the exchange canceled it), canceled (we canceled it), filled, refused (the engine declined to submit it), or ambiguous (the venue outcome could not be established). The two `external event` series count order events arriving for orders this engine did not submit in this process: matched means the event belonged to an order adopted at restart that the engine ledger vouches for; unmatched means it belonged to no such order and was counted and acted on nowhere. Unmatched is not restart-specific and not by itself benign: it counts ANY order event that matches no row the startup pass attached — the account owner's own hand settle in the venue UI, activity nobody sanctioned, and a fill on an order that pass could not see, which on five of the twelve traded legs is every order left resting across a restart. A rise you cannot attribute to something you did is worth investigating. Note also that a restart-adopted order completing counts under filled with no submitted behind it, because these counters reset with the process that submitted them. No alert reads this panel directly. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Fills by liquidity side — the realized maker/taker blend
panels.description: Executed fills split by liquidity side — maker, taker, or no_liquidity_side when the venue did not attribute one. This is the realized maker/taker mix at the venue, not a target. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Fees paid (EUR)
panels.description: Cumulative trading fees paid, in EUR. A fill whose commission could not be denominated in EUR still counts as a fill on the panel beside this one, but does not add to this total. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Position by symbol (base units)
panels.description: Net position held per symbol, in base units. Seeded from the engine journal at startup, so a routine engine restart does not reset it to zero. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Realized PnL (EUR)
panels.description: Cumulative realized profit and loss, in EUR. Unlike the position panel above, this is NOT seeded across an engine restart — it reads zero from process start until the next fill, so a flat line at zero right after a restart is a gap in the record, not a claim that nothing has been made or lost. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Cycles where a book-level limit bound the intended book
panels.description: Cycles where a whole-book limit changed the intended order book before the executor ever saw it — an intent-side signal, not a venue outcome, kept beside the execution panels because it explains apparent gaps between the intended and executed books. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Resting order age — by plan mode
panels.description: How long the engine's current resting order has been at the venue. A rest-hold series is a drill's deliberate artifact, not trading; an execute series is a real trading order and should be short-lived, since its own time box is fifteen minutes. Zero means the engine believes nothing rests — which is not the same as the venue holding nothing, if a cancel never reached it.

panels.title: Venue truth — what the exchange said
Venue snapshot age
panels.description: How long since the last successful venue-truth snapshot. Pages above five hours (one 4h cycle plus an hour of slack) after `for: 5m` — the line this alert's own threshold sits on. Seeded at startup from the newest on-disk snapshot record, so a routine engine restart does not itself age this reading. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Instruments loaded vs expected
panels.description: Ratified instruments successfully loaded from the venue in the last snapshot, against how many the fleet's basket expects. A loaded count below expected does not itself page — the concordance-failures panel beside it is what pages. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

panels.title: Venue concordance failures
panels.description: Ratified instruments that failed runtime concordance in the last snapshot — the venue's own description of an instrument no longer matches what the engine has pinned. Pages above zero after `for: 5m`. Published only by the trading engine on the capture primary.

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.description: Machine the engine runs on. A fixed list, not a query over the engine's own series: such a query empties out in exactly the incident where the engine is dark, which would blank this whole board at once. One option, because running the engine grants the live trade key and that is a security boundary rather than a convenience — a second engine machine is an edit here.
